lessons.claim: Applied the coverage form of the unwired-checker procedure to this repository: 154 error sites in bdbot/, 88 (57 %) never executed under the 1440-test suite, 38 of them in gate modules whose failure refuses a run. Worst: health.Guard's [NUM_NONFINITE] and [NUM_DIVERGE] runtime aborts -- the guards that stop a diverging run -- had never fired in any test, in the same module CLAUDE.md already names for health.gate() having no caller. Also unfired: metrics' rule-7' refusal of composite+implementation_check without a derivation, scales.declare_absent's rule-3 reason requirement, and 9 of intake's L0 schema errors. All 12 load-bearing ones tripped deliberately afterwards fire correctly, so none was dead -- the defect is that nobody had watched them. SECOND-ORDER LESSON, worth more than the list: the first version of the tripping harness counted ANY exception as the gate firing, so 7 of 12 'FIRES' were TypeError from wrong call signatures -- a checker passing for the wrong reason, inside the script written to find checkers that pass for the wrong reason. A negative test must assert the exception TYPE and a distinctive MESSAGE fragment, or it tests nothing.
